messages:
Sam R: kicking off a canary for a P95-driven token shaper on the route-tiering branch. goal: keep p95 <= 120ms for 'chat' routes without tanking throughput. rolling to 20% nodes now.
Anya P: nice — what's the current p95 baseline on canary nodes?
Sam R: baseline on prod for chat-high is ~150ms p95 under typical load. canary baseline (before shaper) was ~148ms.
Mike C: what does the shaper change? quick summary pls.
Sam R: it dynamically adjusts per-request token budget based on route tier + recent p95 signal. reduces max prefix tokens for lower tiers to avoid large microbatches that blow up tail. also bias towards kernel A for short sequences.
Zhen: curious about KV cache behavior — cutting token budgets could reduce KV hit reuse. did you profile KV-hit delta?
Sam R: yes — quick sample: KV hit rate on chat-high fell 2.1 percentage points, chat-low fell 6.7pp. overall token cost dropped ~11%.
Luis: 6.7pp on low routes is ok if latency win is real. what did p95 look like after the shaper?
Sam R: early numbers: on canary nodes after 30m: chat-high p95 -> 118ms, chat-medium -> 132ms (was 145), chat-low -> 140ms (was 160). overall p95 improved.
PerfBot: [ALERT] Canary batcher observed 9% increase in microbatch churn at 10:23:41; tail sample attached.
Anya P: can you paste the config you pushed? want to check the token_budget formula.
Sam R: sure:
```
{
  "shaper_version": "v3",
  "route_tiers": {
    "chat-high": {"base_budget": 64, "p95_target_ms": 120, "priority": 3},
    "chat-medium": {"base_budget": 96, "p95_target_ms": 140, "priority": 2},
    "chat-low": {"base_budget": 128, "p95_target_ms": 180, "priority": 1}
  },
  "adjustment_window_s": 30,
  "max_delta_per_window": 16
}
```
Mike C: where does kernel selection happen in the path? is it after token budget compute or before?
Sam R: budget computed first. small-budget requests prefer kernel-fast (fused attention); larger ones go to kernel-wide which has better throughput but higher startup cost.
Zhen: we should watch kernel switchover latency. profiling showed ~4ms penalty when switching families mid-batch. did you see that?
Sam R: yes, traces show occasional 3-6ms switchover. most of the win still outweighs it.
Luis: any perf regression on dedicated workloads?
Sam R: we ran the nightly perf job against dedicated fixture: no regression in mean latency, p95 improved ~5% for mixed workloads.
Anya P: suggestion — reduce max_delta_per_window to 8 for chat-low to avoid KV hit churn, keep aggressive for chat-high.
Sam R: good call. I'll push a canary patch: set chat-low max_delta_per_window=8 and observe for another hour.
PerfBot: [METRIC] canary-4230123456: p95(chat-high)=116ms, p95(chat-medium)=129ms, p95(chat-low)=138ms at 4230123478
Mike C: if chat-low stays > p95 target we can fallback to baseline budget for that tier only via rollout controller.
Zhen: also add a small hysteresis on kernel selection — require two consecutive windows before switching family to avoid flip-flop.
Sam R: added hysteresis=2 to the rollout plan. pushing now. will post final numbers in 60m. :rocket:
Luis: thanks — if p95 stays under target we can consider a broader rollout and add the shaper to the optimizer suggestions UI.
Anya P: tagging infra to keep an eye on batcher queue depth spikes @eng-infra
Sam R: cc @eng-infra — please watch for queue depth > 600ms on canary nodes.
PerfBot: [INFO] Deploy completed: shaper v3 -> 20% of canary pool at 4230123490
Sam R: thanks everyone. quick checklist for next update: 1) KV hit delta by tier, 2) microbatch churn distribution, 3) kernel switchover counts, 4) p95 per-route. will share artifacts.
Luis: cool — nice work balancing cost + latency.
Anya P: :thumbsup:
